title: A Vow for the Tide
premise: Marine biologist Yara Ishikawa has spent twelve years on a remote research station counting sea turtles, rebuilding a life after a devastating accident took her family and nearly her ability to walk. When her estranged aunt summons her to a family reunion in the coastal town of Merrow's Point, Yara hires local boat captain Theo Vance to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. The fake date turns real by dessert, but Theo is hiding his own secret: he's the anonymous donor whose grant saved her research station years ago. As a development company threatens to bulldoze the nesting beach and her station's funding collapses, Yara must choose between a prestigious fellowship abroad that could save her career and staying to fight for the town, the turtles, and the man who finally sees her whole.
about_author: Zephyrine Yarrow is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who traded lab notebooks for love stories set against salt air and stubborn small towns. She writes romances about people who learn that belonging is not found but built, one brave choice at a time.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the research station at Cormorant Cay, Yara counts loggerhead nests and rehearses excuses not to attend the Ishikawa family reunion. A letter from her aunt arrives demanding her presence. Emotional beat: the quiet ache of a life built entirely around avoidance.

chapters.title: The Captain Who Doesn't Ask Questions
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In Merrow's Point to arrange supplies, she meets Theo Vance, who ferries researchers without prying into their pasts. Impulsively, she offers him money to be her date for one weekend. He surprises her by saying yes—for free. Beat: reckless hope disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo agrees to the arrangement while hiding the truth: his family's marina is failing, and he knows more about Yara's station than she realizes. They rehearse their backstory over bad coffee. Beat: charm layered over guilt, the first crack in his composure.

chapters.title: Arriving as a Couple
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The reunion begins at her aunt's cliffside house; Yara walks in on Theo's arm and feels twelve years of pitying glances shift into curiosity. Her cousin Dana probes their story. Beat: the strange vertigo of being seen as whole.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Over lemon cake, Theo defends Yara against a backhanded toast about her 'brave recovery,' and something unscripted passes between them—a real laugh, a real touch under the table. Beat: the fake date stops being fake, terrifying them both.

chapters.title: One More Weekend
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Neither can end it, so they extend the pretense through the holiday weekend. Theo shows Yara the coves he grew up in; she teaches him to read turtle tracks. Beat: intimacy growing faster than either will admit.

chapters.title: The Letter She Never Sent
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara tells Theo, haltingly, about the accident that killed her parents and ended her fieldwork dreams—why she counts turtles instead of facing people. He listens without flinching. Beat: grief spoken aloud for the first time in years.

chapters.title: Sold Signs on the Shore
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Back at the station, Yara finds surveyors staking the nesting beach—Merrow Point Development has bought the coastline. Her supervisor reveals funding is collapsing too. Beat: the safe world she built begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Benefactor
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo learns the development company is backed by investors including his late father's old partners—and that his own quiet donations once kept Yara's station alive. He says nothing. Beat: guilt calcifying into a lie he can't undo.

chapters.title: A Fellowship Abroad
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A prestigious marine institute in Lisbon offers Yara a two-year fellowship—the career resurrection she thought was impossible forever. Acceptance means leaving before nesting season ends. Beat: hope arriving tangled with an impossible deadline.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings In
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo organizes fishermen and shopkeepers against the development, quietly using his name and savings. Yara joins the fight, and working side by side, they stop pretending this is pretend. First kiss on the dock at dawn. Beat: surrender.

chapters.title: Nesting Season
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The team races to relocate threatened nests before construction permits activate. Yara leads night patrols, feeling more alive than she has in twelve years. Theo helps without being asked. Beat: purpose rediscovered, love deepening in the dark.

chapters.title: Dana Knows
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Cousin Dana visits the station, sees the survey stakes and Yara's fellowship letter, and confronts her: 'You're going to run again.' Yara denies it, furious because it's true. Beat: the mirror she can't turn away from.

chapters.title: The Grant That Saved Everything
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Digging through old station records for the permit fight, Yara discovers the identity of the anonymous donor who funded her first year: T. Vance. Beat: betrayal and tenderness colliding—every kindness suddenly suspect.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Marina
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara demands the truth. Theo admits the donations and confesses he also learned about the development deal weeks ago and stayed silent to protect his failing marina's last investor. Yara walks out. Beat: the price of survival paid in trust.

chapters.title: Lowest Ebb
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo signs away his father's boat to fund the legal challenge alone, then finds Yara's acceptance letter to Lisbon already countersigned. He writes her a letter he doesn't send. Beat: sacrifice without expectation, grief without self-pity.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the county hearing, Yara testifies about the nesting beach with data and, unexpectedly, with heart—speaking publicly for the first time since the accident. The town turns out. The vote is deferred pending environmental review. Beat: finding her voice.

chapters.title: Hatchlings at Midnight
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the deferred beach, the first nest boils over with hatchlings. Yara guides them to the sea alone, weeping, understanding what staying means. Theo appears at the dune line, waiting, not pushing. Beat: clarity in moonlight.

chapters.title: Choosing
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara calls Lisbon and negotiates a compromise: a hybrid appointment with a satellite research site at Merrow's Point—if the beach survives review. Then she goes to Theo, tells him she forgives him, and asks him to choose her openly next time. Beat: love as negotiation, not rescue.

chapters.title: What Theo Builds
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo converts the marina into a community research co-op with Yara's station, putting his name publicly behind the conservation case. His mother, long estranged, returns to help. Beat: redemption made visible, family rebuilt from choice.

chapters.title: The Review
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The environmental review rules in the town's favor; the development withdraws. At a celebration on the beach, Yara introduces Theo to her aunt not as a fake boyfriend but as the real thing. Beat: belonging claimed, loudly, in daylight.

chapters.title: A Vow for the Tide
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, closing with Theo's. One year later: nesting season opens, the co-op thrives, and Yara—no longer counting heartbreaks—counts instead the people gathered on the sand. Theo proposes where they first kissed. Beat: the vow kept, to the tide and to each other.
